newsitem.title: USA: OCC cuts clearing, service fees for U.S. options.
newsitem.headline: OCC cuts clearing, service fees for U.S. options.

text.p: The Options Clearing Corp (OCC), the main U.S. equity options clearing house, said Monday it would cut several clearing and service fees for the balance of the year.
The OCC said clearing fees will be lowered to $0.068 from $0.10 per contract on trades from September 1 through December 31.
Dow Jones index options, expected to debut in October, will have no clearing fee for the first month of trading, a $0.025 per contract fee for the second month and a $0.05 fee for the third month.
After that, the normal fee of $0.10 per contract will be in effect for the new Dow products.
Exercise and data services fees will not be billed for the July 1 to December 31 period and newly set risk-based "haircut" fees will be suspended until the end of the year.
Haircut fees, required of floor traders, are similar to margin required of public customers.
OCC chairman Wayne Luthringshausen said in a statement the OCC fee discounts were instituted because the clearing house has had a successful year thus far.

"Because of continued upside strength in equities and the value of options in protecting portfolio gains, as well as steady increases in the number of institutional and retail investors using options, 1997 has been very successful for OCC," he said.
